what_happened: In job c4w4, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a request about the host's branch rules (the host-rules check). The reading used the classic branch protection endpoint, which answers 403 in this repository because it uses rulesets. The user replaced it. The rules in force are read from GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}, which lists rule objects. Force-pushes are forbidden when a non_fast_forward rule is present. Deletion is forbidden when a deletion rule is present. Up-to-date branches are required when a required_status_checks rule has strict_required_status_checks_policy true. An empty list means no rule is in force. Test fixture replies must have that shape. The correction came before the work went on.
cause: Athena builds the reading from the request and general knowledge of the host's API. Nothing makes it check which mechanism the repository really uses (rulesets or classic protection) or the real shape of the replies before it fixes an endpoint and fixture format in a criterion. Host facts are not recorded where the reading stage can look them up. The wrong endpoint therefore passed into the accepted reading until the user spotted it.
prevention: Record verified host facts in one place the reading stage must consult: which rule mechanism the repo uses, the endpoint that lists the rules in force, and a sample reply for each rule type. Make the reading stage cite that record for any criterion naming a host endpoint or reply shape. If the record lacks the fact, the reading must flag it as unverified instead of assuming classic branch protection. A one-time probe of the host, run at setup and stored, can fill the record.
proposed_request: Build the host-rules check for the records-history work. It must read the rules in force on the main branch with GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}. This repository uses rulesets, and the classic branch protection endpoint answers 403 here. Report force-pushes as forbidden when a non_fast_forward rule is present. Report deletion as forbidden when a deletion rule is present. Report up-to-date branches as required when a required_status_checks rule has parameters.strict_required_status_checks_policy true. An empty list means no rule is in force, and the check must say so. Test it with fixture replies in that shape: all three rules present, each rule alone, an empty list, and a required_status_checks rule with strict false. Add a CHANGELOG entry.
